fields.name: Unthrottled
fields.evidence: bg3.exe+0x1F1C430 (ecl::TimelineDummyAnimationThrottleSystem update, reached from the callback bg3.exe+0x7627B0 set by the registration bg3.exe+0x7490E0) sets the size at +0x0C to 0 every frame, then for every dummy whose wanted state differs from bit 4 of a byte at +0x24 of its animation object: when the wanted state is 1 it appends the 8-byte entity handle of the row here (stride 8, grow helper bg3.exe+0x5C4620) and writes 1 to +0xC0 of the row's first component. The wanted state is 1 when the global switch at ls::GlobalSwitches+0x132E is off, so 1 = animation runs normally. Probe: heap pointer, capacity 8, size 0.

fields.name: Throttled
fields.evidence: Same function: size at +0x1C set to 0 every frame; when the wanted state is 0 (switch on, the system's check object at system+0x10 says yes, and the dummy is not shown / flags at +2,+3 of a 12-byte row are not both 1) the entity handle is appended here and 0 is written to +0xC0 of the row's first component. Probe: heap pointer, capacity 4, size 0.

open_questions: Which of the two arrays means 'throttled' rests on reading the switch at GlobalSwitches+0x132E as 'throttling enabled' and the byte at +0xC0 as 'update enabled'; the consumer (ecl::AnimationUpdateSystem, callback bg3.exe+0x762670) was not read. If the sense is the other way round the two names swap; types and offsets do not change.
